tiles.visual_brief: China Zun has silver-blue glass, strong vertical ribs, a narrow waist, a flared base and a broad concave crown. Elevated and three-quarter CBD views best reveal its vase-like silhouette. Distinguish it from Beijing’s straight-sided China World Trade Center towers, the angular CCTV headquarters and Hong Kong’s unrelated CITIC Tower.
tiles.notes: Six distinct photographs downloaded, decoded, measured and visually checked. Prefer c4 for complete base-to-crown visibility or c5 for a freely licensed portrait. Other candidates have base obstructions. Node downloads substituted for unavailable Python and failing curl TLS.

tiles.visual_brief: Taipei 101 has blue-green glass, eight stacked outward-flaring sections, circular facade medallions and a tiered crown with a long spire. Elephant Mountain provides the classic skyline viewpoint above Xinyi district. Distinguish it from the nearby rectangular Taipei Nan Shan Plaza and Kaohsiung’s forked 85 Sky Tower. The supplied reference is a logo, so identity was checked against the article and identified source photographs.
tiles.notes: Six distinct photographs downloaded, decoded, measured and visually checked; all exceed 2400 pixels on the long side. Prefer c1 for a portrait crop or c2 for native portrait composition. Base obstructions are noted individually.
